analysis.title: 11/2 Mkt Internal Insight: Systematic Selling Exhausted; Real Money Support =>Recovery
key_insights: After two consecutive days of heavy systematic selling, UBS's model estimates Risk Control funds turn to net buyers on Tuesday, while CTA selling is largely complete with limited incremental impact.
The setup points to a potentially quieter Tuesday ahead of the midterm election, with scope for a recovery starting Wednesday post-election.
Friday systematic selling was an estimated $130-150bn: CTA $70-80bn, Risk Control $30-40bn and Leveraged ETFs $30bn.
Monday systematic selling was an estimated $85-115bn: Risk Control $65-85bn, CTA $10-15bn and Leveraged ETFs $10-15bn.
Monday Excess Flow was -$16bn in S&P 500 versus -$53bn in Nasdaq, because most CTA and Leveraged ETF selling and some Risk Control deleveraging were concentrated in Nasdaq.
Friday Excess Flow was -$24bn in S&P 500 versus -$8bn in Nasdaq, as most CTA sell triggers were in S&P 500.
Real money support was strong over the last 3 down days: UBS RMM clients bought the dip all 3 days, foreign-listed US ETFs bought all 3 days, and Multi-Asset Managers / Risk Parity bought Monday.
Equity/bond correlation fell to -46% on a 1-month basis, so Treasuries are again acting as a risk-off asset. UBS sees no sign of a Risk Parity unwind in this sell-off.
Corporate buyback activity is in low seasonality this week and next, and moves to high seasonality of $35-55bn per week starting the week of Nov 16.
Most of Monday's selling came after 1:30pm in orderly, steady flow resembling systematic selling. S&P 500 excess flow was +$15bn until 1:30pm, then -$31bn to the close.
UBS RMM clients continued tax-loss harvesting, selling Tech (Semis, Hardware, IT Services) and buying ETFs (mostly SGOV, QQQ and VOO), with a buy tilt in Software.
Leveraged ETPs sold $12bn on Monday, all in QQQ and Tech exposure. The top stocks to sell by dollars were NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, INTC, AAPL, MSFT, TXN, ADI and MRVL.

sector_views.rationale: Leveraged ETFs sold Tech exposure and RMM clients sold Semis, Hardware and IT Services for tax-loss harvesting. RMM buying was concentrated in ETFs and Software.

risk_factors: A larger decline Tuesday would force Risk Control selling: about $60-65bn at SPX -1.5% and $110-120bn at SPX -2%.
Nasdaq CTA sell triggers at 28050.2 and a medium-term moving-average crossover later this week could add selling.
Buyback support is in low seasonality for the next two weeks.
vol_and_positioning: Risk Control estimated to buy +$10-15bn on Tuesday based on the -0.51% SPX move Monday. After that rebalance, RC exposure is 97%, 69th percentile vs 1Y and 86th percentile vs 5Y.
Risk Control rebalance scenarios for Tuesday: SPX +/-50bps buys $10-15bn, SPX +/-1% sells $15-20bn, SPX -1.5% sells $60-65bn, SPX -2% sells $110-120bn.
CTA global equity exposure is 12% after Monday's rebalance, 9th percentile vs 1Y and 32nd percentile vs 5Y.
Some CTA funds may sell about 50bps before UBS's standard triggers, with footprints of CTA selling around 2:00pm Monday, so remaining CTA sell impact may be small despite the model triggers.
NQ1 CTA triggers: three close sell triggers, two @ 28050.2 (-0.5%) plus a MT MA crossover expected later this week. Five buy triggers sit between +5% and +7%.
RTY1 has no immediate CTA triggers. Four buy triggers sit between +2% and +4% and three sell triggers between -3% and -4%.
UBS RMM net flow Monday was at the 62nd percentile vs 3Y, after being as low as the 28th percentile at 10:05am.
geopolitical: US midterm election on Tuesday, expected to bring a quieter session ahead of it, with recovery possible Wednesday post-election.

tension_points.bull_case: Systematic selling is exhausted, Risk Control turns to buyers, and retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers bought the dip all three days, setting up a recovery from Wednesday post-election.
tension_points.bear_case: If the S&P falls further, Risk Control would sell $60-65bn at SPX -1.5% and $110-120bn at -2%, and buybacks stay in low seasonality for two more weeks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX falling 1.5% or more on Tuesday, which triggers $60-65bn or more of Risk Control selling.

theme_stances.key_argument: Risk Control turns to buyers and CTA selling is largely complete, with real money buying the dip.
theme_stances.evidence: Risk Control should finally turn to buyers tomorrow
